decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposals by reason of design, scale, bulk, massing and location would fail to to enhance local context by delivering buildings and spaces that positively respond to local distinctiveness through their layout, orientation, scale, appearance and shape, with due regard to existing street hierarchy, building types, forms and proportions, or have sufficient distinctive merit so that the development would contribute positively to the character and appearance of the built environment. This would result in an uncharacteristic building that fails relate to its location within the St Helier Estate, contrary to the goals of London Plan 2021 Policy D3, Merton Local Plan 2024 Policies D12.1 & D12.2 and the St Helier Estate Design Guide

Reason : 2 - The proposals by reason of design, scale, bulk, massing and location would represent an unneighbourly and overly dominant form of development that would have an unduly negative impact upon the amenity of neighbouring properties, in particular 6 Bordesley Road, in terms of visual intrusion, loss of outlook and privacy contrary to London Plan 2021 policy D3 and Merton Local Plan 2024 Policy D12.2

Reason : 3 - The proposals by reason of design, layout and ceiling heights and location and size of the proposed bin store would provide a cramped, inaccessible and unsatisfactory standard of internal accommodation exacerbated by a lack of external amenity space with insufficient regard to safety and security that would be detrimental to the amenity and safety of future occupiers, contrary to policies D3, D6 and D7 of the London Plan 2021, Policies H11.1 & D12.3 of the Merton Local Plan 2024 and the Housing Design Standards London Plan Guidance 2023

Reason : 4 - In the absence of a signed s.106 legal agreement to secure affordable housing contributions of �90,000 and in absence of justifying financial viability information, the proposal is contrary to the requirements of Merton Local Plan 2024 policy H11.1

Reason : 5 - In the absence of a signed s.106 legal agreement to secure permit free development to restrict the issue of parking permits, the proposal would have the potential to put undue pressure on local on-street parking spaces within the M2 Controlled Parking Zone. Therefore the proposal is contrary to the requirements of London plan 2021 policy T6.1 and Merton Local Plan 2024 policy T16.3

Reason : 5 - In the absence of a signed s.106 legal agreement to secure permit free development to restrict the issue of parking permits, the proposal would have the potential to put undue pressure on local on-street parking spaces within the M2 Controlled Parking Zone. Therefore the proposal is contrary to the requirements of London plan 2021 policy T6.1 and Merton Local Plan 2024 policy T16.3

Reason : 6 - In the absence of a detailed overheating assessment (e.g. dynamic modelling against CIBSE TM59) and in the absence of a s.106 legal agreement to secure the required carbon offset financial contribution the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposals would meet the sustainable build and energy saving requirements of London Plan 2021(policy SI 2) and the Council's Local Plan 2024 (policies CC2.1 to CC2.6).

Reason : 7 - The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposals would mitigate the loss of trees and vegetation on site or provide measures to improve biodiversity contrary to London Plan 2021 polices G5, G6 & G7 and Merton Local Plan 2024 Policies O15.4 and O15.5.

Reason : 8 - INFORMATIVE
 Note to Applicant
 In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The agent was informed of issues arising during consideration of the application . 
"	The application was considered to be fundamentally contrary to the provisions of the Development Plan and the NPPF, and there were not considered to be any solutions to resolve this conflict. 
"	It is noted that the applicant/agent did not engage in any pre-application discussions.
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
description: ERECTION OF A THREE-STOREY BUILDING WITH 4 x 2 and 2 x 1 -BEDROOM FLATS.
